newsitem.title: AUSTRALIA: Anti-racism protest turns ugly in Australia.
newsitem.headline: Anti-racism protest turns ugly in Australia.

text.p: An anti-racism protest in Australia turned ugly on Saturday when demonstrators tried to break through a police barricade and storm a bookshop run by a right-wing political group.
Police on horseback were called in to keep the 500 protesters at bay, after some tried to breach the barricade set up in front of the shop in suburban Melbourne, police said.

Protesters threw glass bottles, sticks and eggs at the shop run by National Action, accusing the group of being a neo-Nazi organisation trying to foment racial hatred in an economically depressed area of the city.
"They are trying to build on the despair and anger of high unemployment," protester Marcus Banks told reporters.
Police arrested four protesters, charging two young men with assaulting police and a third with unlawful assault. The other man was arrested on an outstanding warrant for another offence.
Police were well prepared for the protest, deploying over 80 officers, including about a dozen on horseback, in case of trouble.
The protest included representatives of Jewish, trade union and homosexual groups and some demonstrators wore face masks.

They marched on the shop after rallying in a nearby park to object to the what they called racist, anti-migration and homophobic messages promoted by National Action. The protest broke up in the early evening. Police reported no injuries.
National Action spokesman Michael Brander defended the group against the charges of racism but said his organisation did not share the protesters' views.
"We don't want an Asian future, no," he told reporters at the front door of the shop.

"We certainly don't want a homosexual future, as they want, and we don't want an internationalist future, and we don't want the government to continue to use left-wing scum to try and silence freedom of speech."

The roudy demonstration comes as opinion polls show an anti-immigration backlash led by maverick politician Pauline Hanson is widely supported. Hanson wants a freeze on immigration, arguing Australia risks being "swamped" by Asians.
